_: The importer's half of K2.3's config schema (libviprs-bench#76, comment 5673286441),
in the shape that comment publishes. It is provisional and lives here only so this
lane's tests can run before #79 merges: at compose it folds into
tools/contract/config.json and this file goes away, which costs no code because
--config already prefers the contract copy when one is there.
Only the blocks the importer reads are filled in. series, defaults, samples.carry
and the verdict palette are the dashboard's and stay K2.3's, with one exception

_outcomes: Three buckets, not causl's two. Upstream refuses the whole import if any cell is
`failed`, because there a failed cell means a runner crashed. Seven cells in the
real capture are `failed` for a fact about the backend (a directory tree has no
root directory to decode) and four are `refused` because allocated_bytes moved
between reps of one generation. Both import as skips carrying their reason, and
`refusing` is empty because the run-level form of causl's check is the one that
survives: at least one cell must be measured.
_publishableProfiles: `ci` proves the harness runs and is never a measurement: three reps, a cut-down
cell list, and an archive entry indistinguishable from a calibrated sweep. It is
refused here rather than at the archive door, because the archive is allowed to
hold it and the page is not.
_archiveBucketFrom: Two fingerprints, because there are two questions. hostFingerprintFrom is the
page's era axis and is K2.3's list. archiveBucketFrom is the producer's own
host8, the last segment of every run id, and it is a different set of fields:
rustc and the scratch filesystem are in it and ncpu is not. The importer derives
the run id from the document and joins it to the archive index, so it has to
reproduce the producer's list exactly; carrying both keeps the era axis right
without making the archive join wrong.
_gatedWhenUncalibrated: One deliberate disagreement with the schema comment, flagged rather than
smuggled. gatedFrom is null because no cell carries a `gated` field, and the
comment then has the importer write null, on the sound argument that 'nobody
said' and 'not gated' are different facts. But verdict.gate only suppresses a
chip on a literal false, so null hands all 284 cells to verdict.regressionPct,
a 10% constant, when 159 of them are low-confidence and the free replicate pair
already moved one metric 53.3%. Chips computed against a guess are the defect
this epic exists to remove, so the importer writes false with a reason while no
calibration exists, and true only where a fitted baseline supplies a tolerance.
Set this to null to get the schema comment's literal behaviour.
_invariantsFilesystemDependent: allocated_bytes is the filesystem's answer to the same bytes, so it moves with
the block size and is compared only between runs on the same fsType and mount
source. In the exact list it would refuse an honest run on another disk.
